pages.title: Execution Boundary and Actor Model
pages.purpose: The celld executor side: Actor serial lifecycle loop, asyncrt as the sole ambient-prism boundary (spawn/select/clocks/Fs), clippy disallowed-methods enforcement, V8-thread vs Actor-domain module split, and cfg-gated simulated asyncrt for deterministic tests.
instructions: Cover how the cfg(celld_internal_tests) + include!(env!()) gates assemble the simulated world from external corpus files, and what a contributor can and cannot see in-tree.
Explain the actor/V8-thread split and why raw tokio/time/randomness calls are lint-forbidden outside asyncrt.

pages.title: Logic Decision Core
pages.purpose: The pure sans-IO decision core: State, Event, Effect, on_event as the sole state transition; the module-per-policy layout (routing, gate, output_gate, pressure, restore, wake, queue, alarm, cron, kv, isolate, schedule, drain, log_tier, log_evict, peer, cell, http, sqlite, sweep, cache, dead_node_reconciliation).
instructions: Ground claims in crates/logic module headers and call sites from the executor; list representative modules by decision area rather than exhaustively.
State that the core contains no async/IO primitives and where that is enforced.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Workspace map: the three crates, the clean-sheet split (logic owns decisions, celld executes effects, ltx provides SQLite replication), dependency direction, and major module ownership.
instructions: Describe the actual dependency direction and file organization; cite Cargo.toml manifests and lib.rs doc comments.
Note the release/lab profiles and the pinned-dependency rationale where they shape architecture.

pages.title: Common Change Guides
pages.purpose: Focused change guides for representative maintenance tasks: adding a policy to the logic core and wiring its executor effect, adding/changing a CELLD_* env var, adding JS API surface, changing bucket layout/protocol, bumping the peer protocol version across a release, and storage-dialect work.
instructions: Keep it a small set of representative tasks; do not enumerate every symbol.
Point each guide at the owning modules and tests to run.

pages.title: Cell-Backed Services: KV, D1, Queues, Alarms, Cron
pages.purpose: Cloudflare services built on cells: reserved classes (__ prefix), KV namespaces, D1 databases, Queues (delivery, leases, retry policy), alarms and wake entries, cron triggers, and Workflows.
instructions: Clarify that these products are implemented as reserved-class cells and their state lives in the same durable machinery.
Cover the operator CLI reach path (operator_cell.rs) for D1/KV/Queue commands.

pages.title: Cells, Ownership, and Fencing
pages.purpose: Cell lifecycle and exclusive ownership: resident/idle/hibernated/inactive states, bucket ownership records via conditional writes, epochs as the data-path fence (cells/<scope>/ltx/e<epoch>), node leases and fleet discovery without consensus, takeover, and self-fencing.
instructions: Cite logic and executor code, not just docs.
Cover self-fencing, dead-node takeover recovery gate, lease renewal, and the hibernate/evict lifecycle; distinguish epoch fencing (data path) from ownership CAS (control path).

pages.title: Durability, Replication, and the Output Gate
pages.purpose: RPO=0 write path: WAL-to-LTX capture, output gate holding egress until a durability proof, bucket tiering vs fleet node-log tier (write-all/ack-all ensemble, log/<node>.json CAS root, hedging, eviction), restore-source safety, and takeover recovery.
instructions: Include the bounded failure semantics: follower failure degrades to bucket proof; recovery from sealed members requires at least one.
Trace the flow from SQL write to ack precisely through code names; include the gray-follower eviction and hedge behavior.

pages.title: HTTP Routing and Peer Tunnel
pages.purpose: Request and control flow across nodes: public vs internal listeners, Worker fetch handling, cell fetch/RPC/WebSocket proxying, the /peer/tunnel upgrade with plain HTTP inside and x-cells-* control headers, retry-safety decisions in logic::routing, and hot-cell admission (CELLD_MAX_CELL_REQUESTS).
instructions: Cover retry safety via the routing decision core.
Explain the v0.4.0 tunnel-based protocol versioning and why mixed-version fleets refuse.

pages.title: JavaScript Runtime and Cell Execution
pages.purpose: Executing Worker code: V8 isolates and pools, isolate heap limits, the RuntimeManager V8 arm, event dispatch through the Actor, hibernatable WebSockets, and the js.rs API modules (bootstrap, storage_ops, r2_ops, websocket, crypto, modules).
instructions: Cite bootstrap/modules/runtime/pool code; state heap-limit failure semantics.
Explain the JS-visible surface (storage, sockets, R2 ops, crypto, modules) and how HostServices injects Actor-reachable state into the raw V8 adapter.

pages.title: The celld-ltx Replication Engine
pages.purpose: The vendored celld-ltx crate: LTX v0.5.2 format, Litestream port scope (db/replica/wal/codec/compactor), ReplicaClient abstraction, bundle objects (celld-original), byte-compatible LZ4 pinning, and compaction levels.
instructions: Describe levels and the additive compaction contract.
Explain the vendoring posture and the bundle/bundle-overlay additions that are celld-original.

pages.title: Object Storage Integration
pages.purpose: The object-store integration: bucket.rs single client with three conditional-write dialects (S3 etag, Azure etag, GCS generation), error contract for CAS, key-prefix multi-fleet sharing, local_store for dev, and the storage requirements (conditional create/overwrite, read-after-write).
instructions: List qualified/unqualified stores exactly as the repository qualifies them.
State the error contract (Ok(None) only for clean rejection; ambiguous errors) and its role in self-fencing.

pages.title: Security Model and Trust Boundaries
pages.purpose: Trust boundaries: one application per fleet, trusted private network requirement, fleet HMAC in fleet/peer_auth.json (body binding, clock limit, replay protection), listener separation, reserved header stripping, and bucket credentials as fleet admin.
instructions: Be explicit about what is NOT authenticated: inner tunnel calls, cell fetch/RPC content.
Cite peer_auth.rs and logic::peer predicates as the fences.

pages.title: Deployments and Local Development
pages.purpose: Application lifecycle: `celld deploy` (Wrangler config subset, esbuild), deploy/current.json pointer, generation adoption and draining, resident-object safe points and forced moves, and the local `celld dev` supervisor with its SQLite-backed local object store.
instructions: Cover dev's local_store rationale and watcher behavior.
Explain the two-step adoption (build beside, switch new requests) and forcing semantics.

pages.title: Fleet Operations and Configuration
pages.purpose: Running nodes: configuration surface (CELLD_* variables and flags), startup listener policy, memory pressure and shedding (logic::pressure, cgroup working set, V8 heap limits), graceful shutdown/handoff with drain token, readiness gate, rolling-update compatibility exceptions, and operator commands (diagnose, cell list, d1/kv/queue CLIs).
instructions: Cover cgroup working-set math and the cap-vs-threshold release hysteresis.
Ground every setting name/default in env_vars.rs, cli_options.rs, machine.rs, and docs; flag any discrepancy between docs and code as uncertainty.

pages.title: Telemetry and Observability
pages.purpose: Observability: opt-in telemetry (CELLD_OTEL), Parquet bucket sink vs hand-encoded OTLP sink, span model and W3C traceparent propagation, log capture pipeline, and reading /state and log output during incidents.
instructions: Cover span/log correlation and the manual OTLP encoder tradeoff.
Include the structured node-log line format and /state counters where they are the debugging surface.

pages.title: Testing Strategy
pages.purpose: How correctness is defended: the four layers (differential conformance vs workerd, TLA+ model checking, deterministic simulation of the logic core with seeded adversarial schedules, live-fleet fault injection), and how in-tree tests are gated and run (cargo test, cfg(celld_internal_tests), external corpus env vars).
instructions: Document the in-repo seams; state plainly that spec/simulation corpora live outside this repository where the code shows include!(env!(...)) gates.
Explain mutation-testing-of-checkers and pinned verdicts as described in docs/testing.md.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Task-oriented entry point: what celld is, how to build/test locally, run `celld dev`, deploy, and route to the right wiki page for maintenance work.
instructions: List the exact commands the repo itself shows (README, docs, Cargo.toml profiles, workflows); do not invent CI or deployment details.
Route readers by task: build, run dev, deploy, operate, debug, test, change.
